mainTopic: שבועת שקר vs. שבועת שוא: which לאו each breaks, and when swearing gets lashes
overview: This amud first finishes explaining a ברייתא that called שבועת שוא and שבועת שקר 'one,' and gives a second answer: both bring a קרבן, following רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא then seems to define שבועת שקר differently from רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא answers by reading it as 'he swears and later goes against it.' Next, רבין reports in רבי יוחנן's name that a false oath about the past breaks 'לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר,' a broken future oath breaks 'לא יחל דברו,' and a שבועת שוא is swearing against a known fact. רב פפא says רבי אבהו only worked this out by inference. The starting point is a rule that there are no lashes for a לאו without an action, except for swearing and two other cases. The גמרא finds the source for lashes for swearing in 'כי לא ינקה ה׳,' and for שבועת שקר in the second 'לשוא.' רבי אבהו shows that the false oath that gets lashes must be about the past, and רבא explains that this is because it is modeled on שבועת שוא. Finally, רבי ירמיה challenges this from a משנה, and the גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who excludes past-tense oaths only from the קרבן, not from lashes.

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches what אביי will explain
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an earlier answer: the ברייתא that calls שוא and שקר 'one' is teaching us the point that אביי explains below.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us like he answers him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its first answer to the ברייתא that called שבועת שוא and שבועת שקר 'one.' It says the ברייתא is teaching the point that אביי explains later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the גמרא was trying to explain why the ברייתא would call two different oaths 'one.' This line closes that answer by pointing ahead to אביי's explanation, so the ברייתא is not seen as erasing the difference between the two oaths.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us / this comes to tell us

phrases.english: It teaches us
as he answers him.
phrases.notes: This points ahead to the answer אביי gives later on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the first answer to the ברייתא that calls שוא and שקר 'one,' which started before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the ברייתא comes to teach
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's word 'one' teaches the point אביי explains. It does not mean the two oaths are the same in every way.

steps.title: Second answer: both oaths bring a קרבן, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: A second way to explain the ברייתא: שוא and שקר are 'one' because a קרבן is brought for both, and this follows רבי עקיבא, who treats past-tense oaths like future-tense oaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: just as one brings a קרבן for a false oath, so one brings a קרבן for an oath in vain. And this follows רבי עקיבא, who makes a person liable for an oath about the past just like an oath about the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the ברייתא. 'One' means the two oaths share the same law: a person brings a קרבן for each of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קרבן is tied to oaths about the future. רבי עקיבא holds that an oath about the past also brings a קרבן. Under his view, the ברייתא can say שוא is like שקר in bringing a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (an alternative answer)
An offering brought for the sin

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
just as one brings an offering for a false oath,
so one brings an offering for an oath in vain;
and this follows Rabbi Akiva,
who makes one liable for the past just as for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the same ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading 'one' as a shared law (bringing a קרבן), not as the same oath
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא: a קרבן is brought for שוא just like for שקר.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines שבועת שקר differently
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines שבועת שוא as swearing against a known fact, and שבועת שקר as 'swearing to contradict.' This seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's definitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Which is an oath in vain? One who swears to change what is known to people. A false oath: one who swears to contradict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן's way of separating a false oath from an oath in vain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording for שבועת שקר, 'swearing to contradict,' does not fit the categories רבי יוחנן set up. So it looks like the ברייתא defines the oaths differently than he does.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath in vain, a pointless or obviously false oath

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Which is an oath in vain?
One who swears to change what is known to people.
phrases.notes: For example, swearing that something everyone knows is real is not real.

phrases.english: A false oath: one who swears to contradict!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge, this time against רבי יוחנן's definitions.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's distinction between שבועת שקר and שבועת שוא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא defines שבועת שקר with wording that does not match רבי יוחנן's categories.

steps.title: Read it as 'swears and then contradicts'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא as 'swears and contradicts': he swears, and afterwards acts against his oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: he swears and contradicts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how we read one word in the ברייתא so that it no longer clashes with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'swears to contradict,' read 'swears and contradicts.' That describes someone who makes an oath and later acts against it. Read this way, the ברייתא does not argue with רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אימא' means the גמרא is fixing how the ברייתא should be read. It is not bringing a new opinion.

phrases.english: Say: he swears and contradicts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing how the ברייתא's wording is read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא defines שבועת שקר in a way that clashes with רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means someone who swears and afterwards acts against the oath, so there is no clash.

steps.title: רבין's version of רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in רבי יוחנן's name: a false oath about the past is שקר and breaks 'לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר.' A broken oath about the future breaks 'לא יחל דברו.' A שבועת שוא is swearing against a known fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי ירמיה, in the name of רבי אבהו, in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'I ate' or 'I did not eat' (if untrue) is a false oath, and its warning is from 'Do not swear falsely by My name.' 'I will eat' or 'I will not eat' (if broken) breaks 'He shall not break his word.' And which is an oath in vain? Swearing to change what is known to people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבין's report of רבי יוחנן's teaching. It sorts the oaths into three types and gives the source for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false oath about the past ('I ate') is a lie at the moment it is said, so it falls under 'לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר.' An oath about the future ('I will eat') only becomes a sin when he breaks it, so it falls under 'לא יחל דברו.' A שבועת שוא is its own category: swearing against something everyone already knows is true.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Its warning / the לאו that forbids it
Do not swear falsely by My name
He shall not break his word

steps.whatToRemember: Past-tense false oath = שקר, which breaks 'לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר.' Future oath that is broken = 'לא יחל דברו.' שבועת שוא = swearing against a known fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the basic map of oath sins: which לאו applies to each kind of oath, and how a שבועת שוא is different from a שבועת שקר.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
Rabbi Yirmeya said
that Rabbi Abbahu said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
'I ate' or 'I did not eat' is a false oath,
and its warning is from 'You shall not swear by My name falsely.'
'I will eat' or 'I will not eat':
he transgresses 'He shall not break his word.'
And which is an oath in vain?
One who swears to change what is known to people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different report (רבין's) of רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A past-tense false oath breaks 'לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר.' A broken future oath breaks 'לא יחל דברו.' A שבועת שוא is swearing against a known fact.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי אבהו's statement was inferred, not stated outright
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the statement רבי אבהו reported from רבי יוחנן was not said in so many words. It was worked out from a broader rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That statement of רבי אבהו was not said explicitly. Rather, it was said by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells us that רבי אבהו's report of רבי יוחנן was not a direct quote. The גמרא is setting up the next step, where it shows the general rule this report was drawn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן never directly said what רבי אבהו reported. רבי אבהו worked it out from a wider rule that רבי יוחנן passed on. The next step brings that rule, and the steps after it show how רבי אבהו drew his conclusion from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, said in so many words
By inference, worked out from a general rule

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This statement of Rabbi Abbahu
was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference;

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the origin of רבי אבהו's report of רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו's statement in רבי יוחנן's name was inferred from a general rule, not said outright.

steps.title: The general rule: no lashes for a prohibition without action, except three cases
steps.stepSummary: A long chain of names passes down רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule: a לאו with an action gets lashes, and a לאו without an action does not. The exceptions are swearing, substituting a קרבן animal, and cursing with God's Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב עמרם, in the name of רב יצחק, in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי: For every prohibition in the Torah, if it involves an action, one gets lashes; if it involves no action, one does not get lashes. The exceptions are one who swears, one who substitutes an animal, and one who curses his fellow with God's Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the general rule that רבי אבהו drew his statement from. The rule says lashes come only for a לאו with an action, and it lists three exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swearing is only speech, so normally it would get no lashes. Since the rule lists swearing as an exception, a person who swears does get lashes. This rule alone is not רבי אבהו's whole inference: the גמרא first finds the פסוק behind it, and then רבי אבהו works out which kind of oath it must mean (steps 14–20).

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that involves a physical action
One who swaps a regular animal for a קרבן animal
Cursing another person using God's Name

steps.whatToRemember: Normally there are no lashes for a לאו that has no action. Swearing is one of three exceptions.

phrases.english: As Rav Idi bar Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם, אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rav Amram said, Rav Yitzchak said,
Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
Every prohibition in the Torah:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה לוֹקִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: a prohibition that involves an action, one is lashed for it,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו;
phrases.english: and one that does not involve an action, one is not lashed for it;
except for one who swears, and one who substitutes,
phrases.notes: Substituting means swapping a regular animal for one already set aside as a קרבן (ויקרא 27:10).

phrases.english: and one who curses his fellow with the Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the general rule that step 6 said רבי אבהו's statement was drawn from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no lashes for a לאו without an action, except for swearing, substituting a קרבן animal, and cursing with God's Name.

steps.title: What is the source that one who swears gets lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source that a person who swears falsely gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who swears: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the Torah teaches that swearing is an exception that gets lashes. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule listed swearing as an exception, but an exception needs a source. The גמרא now looks for a פסוק showing lashes even though no action was done.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: One who swears: from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first exception in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches lashes for a person who swears, even without an action.

steps.title: From 'כי לא ינקה': Heaven does not clear him, but בית דין does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, learns from 'כי לא ינקה' that the heavenly court does not clear the sinner. The earthly court lashes him, and that clears him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: The verse says, 'You shall not take the name of ה׳ your God in vain, for He will not clear.' The heavenly court does not clear him, but the earthly court lashes him and clears him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from the עשרת הדברות. The words 'לא ינקה' are read as hinting that an earthly punishment can clear him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only Heaven will not clear him. That suggests the earthly בית דין can clear him, and it does so through lashes. This gives the source for lashes for swearing, even though swearing is only speech.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,
the verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת שֵׁם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַשָּׁוְא
phrases.english: 'You shall not take the name of ה׳ your God in vain,
for He will not clear [him]':

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה אֵין מְנַקִּין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: the heavenly court does not clear him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה מַלְקִין אוֹתוֹ וּמְנַקִּין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: but the earthly court lashes him and clears him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי לא ינקה' means only Heaven does not clear him. The earthly בית דין lashes him and so clears him.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe the verse means he is never cleared at all
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי whether 'לא ינקה' simply means the sinner is never cleared at all, which would leave no hint of earthly lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying: 'He will not be cleared' at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the reading in step 9. He suggests the פסוק might mean no one can ever clear this sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לא ינקה' means he is never cleared, the פסוק says nothing about earthly lashes. Then the source for lashes from step 9 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:
'He will not be cleared' at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לא ינקה' refers only to the heavenly court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words could just as easily mean he is never cleared. Then there is no hint of earthly lashes.

steps.title: The word ה׳ limits it: only ה׳ does not clear him
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק adds the word 'ה׳'. That shows only ה׳ does not clear him, while the earthly court lashes and clears him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were written only 'for he will not be cleared,' it would be as you say. Now that it is written 'for ה׳ will not clear,' it is ה׳ who does not clear him. But the earthly court lashes him and clears him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב פפא's reading by pointing to the word 'ה׳' in the פסוק. That word shows the 'not clearing' belongs only to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'ה׳', the פסוק could mean no one ever clears him. Because it says ה׳ will not clear him, the extra word limits the 'not clearing' to Heaven. That leaves room for בית דין to clear him through lashes.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'ה׳' in 'כי לא ינקה ה׳' is the key. Only Heaven refuses to clear him, so the earthly lashes do clear him.

phrases.english: If it were written 'for he will not be cleared,'
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב פפא, even though the text doesn't name him.

phrases.english: it would be as you say;
now that it is written 'for ה׳ will not clear,'
it is ה׳ who does not clear him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה מַלְקִין אוֹתוֹ וּמְנַקִּין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: but the earthly court lashes him and clears him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of the exact wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא ינקה' could mean he is never cleared by anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the פסוק names 'ה׳', only Heaven does not clear him. The earthly court lashes and clears him.

steps.title: We have a source for שבועת שוא; what about שבועת שקר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the source so far covers שבועת שוא. It now asks for a source for lashes for a שבועת שקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for a vain oath. From where do we know it for a false oath?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the פסוק 'לא תשא לשוא' covers only a vain oath. It asks how we know the same for a false oath, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'שוא', which covers a שבועת שוא. A שבועת שקר is a different kind of oath, so it needs its own source for lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A vain oath, swearing against a known fact

phrases.english: We have found a vain oath;
a false oath, from where do we derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא, שְׁבוּעַת שֶׁקֶר מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the search for a source from שבועת שוא to שבועת שקר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a שבועת שקר also gets lashes.

steps.title: 'לשוא' is written twice, so the second one teaches שבועת שקר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן himself says 'לשוא' appears twice in the פסוק. Since the second one is not needed for שבועת שוא, it is applied to שבועת שקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן himself said: 'In vain' is written twice. If it is not needed for a vain oath, apply it to a false oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his own source. The extra 'לשוא' in the פסוק teaches lashes for a שבועת שקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat a word for nothing. One 'לשוא' already covers a שבועת שוא, so the extra one is moved over to teach about a שבועת שקר.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter

steps.whatToRemember: Lashes for both kinds of oath come from 'לא תשא': 'כי לא ינקה ה׳' teaches the lashes, and the second 'לשוא' brings in שבועת שקר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan himself said:
'In vain,' 'in vain,' two times;
phrases.notes: The same פסוק says 'לשוא' twice: once in 'לא תשא… לשוא' and again in 'את אשר ישא את שמו לשוא'.

phrases.english: if it is not needed for the matter of a vain oath,
apply it to the matter of a false oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second 'לשוא' is extra for שבועת שוא, so it is applied to שבועת שקר.

steps.title: רבי אבהו asks what case of false oath gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks what exact case of שבועת שקר is meant when רבי יוחנן says it gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו discussed it: this false oath, what kind of case is it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו asks which case of שבועת שקר gets lashes based on the extra 'לשוא'. This question sets up the next few steps, where he tests possible cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave a source for lashes for שבועת שקר. But that word 'false oath' can describe several cases, so רבי אבהו wants to pin down which one the source is really talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: And he discussed it, he looked into it
A false oath, one that turns out untrue
What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu discussed it:
This false oath, what are its circumstances?
phrases.notes: "This" false oath is the one from step 13, the one learned from the second 'לשוא'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the case covered by the source for שבועת שקר given in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case of שבועת שקר that gets lashes through the extra 'לשוא'.

steps.title: Not an oath not to eat that he then broke
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is 'I swear I won't eat,' and then he ate. This is rejected, because eating is an action, so it is an ordinary prohibition done with an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means 'I swear I won't eat' and he ate, that is a prohibition done with an action!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו tries the first possible case, a future oath not to eat that he breaks by eating. He pushes it away right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking this oath means actually doing something (eating). That makes it a normal לאו שיש בו מעשה, which gets lashes under the ordinary rules. So this cannot be the special case that needed the extra 'לשוא'.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, if we suggest
A prohibition that is broken by doing an action

phrases.english: If we say: "an oath that I will not eat,"
and he ate —
that is a prohibition that involves an action!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the special source is about a future 'I won't eat' oath.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is already a לאו שיש בו מעשה, so it gets lashes anyway and does not fit as the special case.

steps.title: Not an oath to eat that he failed to keep
steps.stepSummary: The second suggestion is 'I swear I will eat,' and then he did not eat. This is challenged, because רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both rule there are no lashes in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe he said 'I swear I will eat' and didn't eat. But is that person lashed? It was taught that if he swore 'I will eat this loaf today' and the day passed without his eating it, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say he is not lashed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו tries a second case, an oath to eat that is broken by not eating. He knocks it down with a known ruling that such a person gets no lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the special source were about this case, it would give lashes. But רבי יוחנן himself, along with ריש לקיש, says there are no lashes here. So this case cannot be what רבי יוחנן meant.

phrases.english: But rather, where he said: "an oath that I will eat,"
and he did not eat —
is such a person lashed?!
But wasn't it stated:
"an oath that I will eat this loaf today,"
and the day passed and he did not eat it —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say:
he is not lashed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first case in step 15, tries the opposite case and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the special source is about a future 'I will eat' oath that was not kept.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rule there are no lashes for exactly this case, so the source giving lashes cannot be talking about it.

steps.title: The two reasons there are no lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why each one says no lashes. רבי יוחנן: it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה. ריש לקיש: the warning is a התראת ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is not lashed because it is a prohibition with no action, and no one gets lashes for a prohibition with no action. ריש לקיש says he is not lashed because the warning was an uncertain one, and an uncertain warning does not count as a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the ruling just quoted. Both agree there are no lashes, but each has his own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason is that not eating is not an action, and lashes need an action. ריש לקיש's reason is that during the day, nobody can know if he will still eat later. So any warning given to him is uncertain, and lashes need a clear warning. רבי יוחנן's reason is the one that matters for רבי אבהו's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition broken without doing any action
An uncertain warning, given when it is not clear yet that a sin will happen
The warning that must be given before a sin for there to be lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Both say 'not lashed,' but for different reasons. Don't mix them up: רבי יוחנן = no action; ריש לקיש = uncertain warning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says he is not lashed —

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: because it is a prohibition that has no action,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: and for any prohibition with no action, we do not give lashes.
And Reish Lakish says he is not lashed —
because it is an uncertain warning,
phrases.notes: While the day is still going, he could still eat the loaf, so any warning can't be sure he's sinning.

phrases.english: and an uncertain warning is not called a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ruling used to reject the case in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. ריש לקיש: no lashes when the warning is a התראת ספק.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: it means a false oath about the past
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו concludes that the case is a past-tense oath: 'I ate' or 'I did not eat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: let it be about 'I ate' or 'I did not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers his own question from step 14. The lashes for שבועת שקר are for a false oath about something in the past.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both future cases have been ruled out. So the special source must be about a lie about the past, like swearing 'I ate' when he didn't. Even though no action is done there, the extra 'לשוא' gives lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be about, it must refer to

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
Let it be about "I ate" and "I did not eat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both future cases are rejected, gives the case that remains.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שבועת שקר that gets lashes is a false oath about the past, like 'I ate' or 'I did not eat.'

steps.title: Why is a past oath different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a past-tense false oath gets lashes when it also has no action.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a past oath gets lashes even though no action is done. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and swearing 'I ate' falsely also has no real action. So why should it be treated differently from the 'I will eat' case?

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference? Why is this case different?

phrases.english: And what is different?
phrases.notes: He means: why does a past oath get lashes when the 'I will eat' oath doesn't, though neither has an action?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the answer in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a past-tense false oath gets lashes even though it is also a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

steps.title: רבא: the Torah links false oaths to vain oaths, which are about the past
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the Torah made שבועת שקר similar to שבועת שוא. Just as שבועת שוא is about the past, the שבועת שקר that gets lashes is about the past too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the Torah clearly included a false oath that is similar to a vain oath. Just as a vain oath is about the past, a false oath is also about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers why only a past oath is included. The extra 'לשוא' brings in only false oaths that resemble a vain oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for שבועת שקר comes from the second 'לשוא', the word about vain oaths. So it only covers oaths that look like a vain oath. A vain oath is about something already known, which means the past. This special Torah inclusion gives lashes even without an action.

keyTerms.meaning: A vain oath, a pointless oath about something obviously true or false

steps.whatToRemember: The lashes for שבועת שקר learned from the second 'לשוא' apply only to a false oath about the past, because it is modeled on שבועת שוא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יוחנן can give lashes for שבועת שקר even though he holds no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. The past oath is a special inclusion by the Torah.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Torah clearly included
a false oath that is similar to a vain oath,
phrases.notes: This is the second 'לשוא' from step 13, which brings in false oaths alongside vain ones.

phrases.english: just as a vain oath is about the past,
so too a false oath is also about the past.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'לשוא' includes only a false oath that is like a vain oath. Since a vain oath is about the past, only a past false oath is included, and it gets lashes even without an action.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה challenges from the משנה on repeated oaths
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a משנה about someone who swears three times not to eat a loaf and then eats it. He is liable only once, and the משנה calls this the שבועת ביטוי that gets lashes for doing it on purpose and a קרבן עולה ויורד for doing it by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה challenged רבי אבהו: 'I swear I won't eat this loaf,' 'I swear I won't eat it,' 'I swear I won't eat it,' and then he ate it, he is liable only once. This is a שבועת ביטוי, where one is lashed for doing it on purpose and brings a sliding-scale offering for doing it by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה starts an objection against רבי אבהו by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the challenge, and the next step spells out the exact point of the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה talks about future oaths ('I won't eat') and says a שבועת ביטוי gets lashes when broken on purpose. רבי ירמיה brings this to test רבי אבהו's understanding of which oaths get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath said out loud about doing or not doing something
A sliding-scale offering whose cost depends on how wealthy the person is

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection to Rabbi Abbahu:
"An oath that I will not eat this loaf,"
"an oath that I will not eat it," "an oath that I will not eat it,"
and he ate it — he is liable only once.
This is the oath of utterance,
for which one is liable to lashes when it is done on purpose
and to a sliding-scale offering when it is done by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's conclusion from steps 18 and 20 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's view of which oaths get lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about future oaths calls this case a שבועת ביטוי that gets lashes when broken on purpose. רבי ירמיה uses this to test רבי אבהו, and step 22 spells out the exact point of the clash.

steps.title: What does 'this is' come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה completes his challenge. The משנה's words 'זו היא' seem to exclude a past-tense oath from lashes, which goes against רבי אבהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה says 'this is' the oath, what is it trying to leave out? Isn't it leaving out an oath like 'I ate' or 'I did not eat,' to teach that a person does not get lashes for it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה points to the words 'this is' in the משנה from Step 21. He argues that they exclude past-tense oaths, so such oaths would not get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו said in Step 18 that lashes are given for a past-tense oath. The משנה is about a future oath ('I will not eat this loaf') and says 'this is' the oath that gets lashes. That sounds like only future oaths get lashes, and past-tense oaths do not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is'. A limiting phrase that sounds like it excludes other cases

phrases.english: "This is"
phrases.notes: These are the words from the משנה quoted in step 21: 'this is the שבועת ביטוי.'

phrases.english: comes to exclude what?
Is it not to exclude "I ate" and "I did not eat"
that he does not get lashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי ירמיה's challenge that began with quoting the משנה in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's view (Step 18) that the oath which gets lashes is a past-tense oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limiting phrase 'זו היא' in the משנה implies that past-tense oaths are excluded from lashes.

steps.title: It excludes past-tense oaths only from the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'זו היא' excludes past-tense oaths from the קרבן עולה ויורד, not from lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It excludes 'I ate' and 'I did not eat' from a קרבן. This is the oath for which you bring a קרבן עולה ויורד if you break it by mistake. But for 'I ate' or 'I did not eat,' no קרבן is brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. 'This is' does not refer to the lashes. It refers to the קרבן part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions two things: lashes and a קרבן. The גמרא says the exclusion only applies to the קרבן. So a past-tense oath brings no קרבן, but it can still get lashes, and רבי אבהו's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: From an offering, meaning from the obligation to bring a קרבן
Its unintentional violation, breaking it by mistake
A sliding-scale offering whose cost depends on how wealthy the person is

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'this is' does not take away lashes from a past-tense oath. It only takes away the קרבן.

phrases.english: No, it is to exclude "I ate" and "I did not eat" from an offering
This is the one for which, when broken by mistake,
one brings a sliding-scale offering,
but "I ate" and "I did not eat" do not.
phrases.notes: Meaning: for these past-tense oaths there is no קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge by narrowing what the exclusion refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the scope of the limiting phrase: it applies to the קרבן, not to lashes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זו היא' excludes past-tense oaths from lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זו היא' excludes past-tense oaths only from the קרבן עולה ויורד.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the משנה as following רבי ישמעאל: a קרבן is brought only for oaths about the future, but lashes are given even for past-tense oaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who says a person is only obligated to bring a קרבן for oaths about the future. But he does get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by naming whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that the קרבן for oaths applies only to future oaths. That explains why the משנה excludes past-tense oaths from the קרבן. Lashes are a separate law, so a false past-tense oath still gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The future, what is yet to come

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, a false oath about the past ('I ate' or 'I did not eat') brings no קרבן but does get lashes. The משנה's 'זו היא' only excludes the קרבן, so רבי אבהו's view survives the challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This separates the two punishments for a false oath: the קרבן and lashes do not always apply to the same cases.

phrases.english: And it is the view of רבי ישמעאל,
who says: one is not obligated
phrases.notes: He means obligated to bring a קרבן.

phrases.english: except for the future;
but he does get lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 23 by naming the תנא whose view the משנה follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to deny lashes for past-tense oaths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל: no קרבן for past-tense oaths, but lashes still apply.
